title: Nightly Degradation Hunting and Reconciliation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes the nightly degradation hunting workflow used by Platform Operators to detect, triage, and reconcile transient degradations that appear in overnight windows (00:00–06:00 PT). These degradations commonly affect tail latency, batcher throughput, or KV/prefix cache hit rates and can silently erode customer SLAs and increase unit cost. The goal is to provide a deterministic, operator-friendly checklist that is reproducible and minimizes noisy escalations while ensuring correct root cause capture and remediation.

When to run this playbook
- Automated nightly scan alerts have fired: ALERT_NIGHTLY_DEGRADATION or ALERT_BATCHER_ANOMALY.
- Operator receives a customer-facing signal referencing increased 99p latency that only happens during off-peak hours.
- Postmortem follow-up to reconcile partial fixes deployed during a maintenance window.

Owner and Roles
- Primary oncall: Platform Operator (platform-oncall rota) — executes hunting workflow and begins reconciliation.
- Secondary: Runtime SRE — deep investigation if runtime kernel / GPU interference suspected.
- Escalation: Serving Runtime Lead (pager if incident qualifies as Sev-2).
- Stakeholder notifications: Product & Customer Success if customer-facing impact identified.

SLOs and Detection Thresholds
- Tail latency SLO: 99th-token-latency < 300ms (hosted API). Alert if 99p increases > 20% vs rolling 7-day baseline and is sustained > 10 minutes.
- Error rate SLO: 5xx < 0.1% of requests. Alert on 5x baseline sustained 5 minutes.
- Cache hit SLO: KV-prefix-cache hit rate >= 92%. Alert if hit rate drops by > 8 percentage points vs baseline.
- Cost signal: token-cost-per-1M > $X (alerting group) — investigate if simultaneous with latency/caching regressions.

Prerequisites and Access
1) Access to Operator Dashboard (Grafana): dashboards/operator/nightly-hunting.
2) Access to telemetry query API: https://internal-api.redwood/platform/telemetry/query (use service account key).
3) Access to key infra services: runtime-api, prefix-cache, batcher, prefetch-coordinator.
4) JIRA: PLATFORM-ops project to file tickets and reconcile fixes.

Runbook: Nightly Hunting Workflow (step-by-step)
1) Acknowledge alert and capture immediate context
   - Take the alert page URL, time range, and affected metric. Do not immediately escalate.
   - Record in JIRA: create a ticket with summary: [nightly-hunt] <short description> and label nightly-hunt.
2) Quick triage (first 5 minutes)
   - Open Grafana dashboard: dashboards/operator/nightly-hunting, set window to alerted interval + 30m before/after.
   - Check three canonical panels: 99p latency (runtime-api), KV-prefix-cache hit rate, batcher throughput and queue length.
   - Compare to rolling-7d baseline panels on the same dashboard (panels include baseline ribbon).
3) Run targeted telemetry queries (examples below)
   - Query 1: compare 99p token latency by region (SQL-like):

     SELECT region, percentile(0.99, token_latency_ms) AS p99
     FROM telemetry.tokens
     WHERE service = 'runtime-api' AND time BETWEEN '2025-11-01T00:00:00Z' AND '2025-11-01T06:00:00Z'
     GROUP BY region

   - Query 2: cache hit rate delta:

     SELECT window, sum(hit)/sum(hit+miss) AS hit_rate
     FROM telemetry.prefix_cache
     WHERE key_namespace = 'kv-prefix' AND time BETWEEN :start AND :end
     GROUP BY window

4) Correlate signals
   - If p99 increase aligns with cache hit rate drop -> suspect cache churn or cold start event.
   - If p99 increase aligns with increased queue length and decreased batch sizes -> suspect batcher misconfiguration or prefetch drop.
   - If gradients across regions differ -> suspect regional capacity or network egress issue.
5) Run quick mitigation (if safe)
   - If cache hit rate low and prefetch-coordinator shows large rebalancing events: trigger prefetch throttle: 

     curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/control/prefetch -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" -d '{"action":"throttle","cohort":"nightly","duration_s":900}'

   - If batcher queue length is high due to small batch sizes, increase the batcher target size by +20% using operator CLI (safe only during low traffic windows):

     cli operator batcher update --pool gpu-pool-2 --target-batch-size 64

6) If mitigation applied, monitor for 15 minutes. If telemetry returns to baseline, document change and close the JIRA with reconciliation notes.

Investigation playbook (deeper)
- Check deploy history: /releases/service/runtime-api for any canary/rollouts in previous 1–24 hours.
- Kernel / GPU interference: reference runbook: eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/gpu-interference-detection-and-mitigation-playbook-2026. Run the profiling script: /opt/operator/tools/gpu-interf-check.sh --since 6h.
- Telemetry ingestion gaps: confirm no ingestion-latency anomalies in agent pipeline (kafka consumer lag > 30s).
- Cross-tenant noisy neighbor: run tenant-usage top-10 query to see if a tenant spiked token volume during window.

Dashboard and Alerts to check or create
- dashboards/operator/nightly-hunting (primary)
  - Panels: p99-token-latency (by region), batcher-queue-length, batcher-batch-size-distribution, prefix-cache-hit-rate, token-cost-per-1m, runtime-errors-5xx.
- Alert rules (recommended):
  1) ALERT_NIGHTLY_DEGRADATION: p99 > baseline*1.2 for > 10m during 00:00-06:00 local. Severity: P2. Pager: platform-oncall.
  2) ALERT_BATCHER_ANOMALY: average batch size drops > 30% and queue length increases > 200 items for > 5m. Severity: P3. Slack only.

Metric queries and dashboards (examples)
- PromQL example for p99 comparison:

  (quantile_over_time(0.99, token_latency_ms[1h]) / avg_over_time(token_latency_ms[7d])) > 1.2

- SQL example for tenant spike:

  SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as tokens_per_window
  FROM telemetry.usage
  WHERE time BETWEEN :start AND :end
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  ORDER BY tokens_per_window DESC
  LIMIT 10

Operator reconciliation checklist (table)
- Use this table as a copyable checklist when closing tickets.

  | Step | Action | Evidence to attach |
  |------|--------|-------------------|
  | 1 | Create JIRA | JIRA id and alert URL |
  | 2 | Triage dashboard | Screenshots + time-series gifs |
  | 3 | Run queries | Query text + results (CSV) |
  | 4 | Apply mitigation (if any) | Command run + operator logs |
  | 5 | Monitor | 15m post-mitigation graph panels |
  | 6 | Reconcile & close | Root cause hypothesis + remediation steps |

Post-incident reconciliation and telemetry artifacts
- Always attach the following to the JIRA: alert payload, Grafana snapshots, the telemetry queries used, and any CLI commands executed. For mitigations, attach the operator logs from /var/log/operator/actions/<jira-id>.log.
- If a code/config change was rolled, include a link to the PR and deployment tag.

Escalation criteria
- Escalate to Runtime SRE if any of the following are true:
  - p99 latency remains > 2xSLO and affects > 10% of customer requests for > 30 minutes.
  - Error rate > 1% sustained 10 minutes.
  - Evidence of kernel/GPU preemption or driver failure.
- If customer has opened a ticket, CC Customer Success and attach the stabilized mitigation steps with expected ETA for full remediation.

Retrospective and Continuous Improvement
- For every nightly-hunt that results in operator mitigation, schedule a 30-minute retro within 3 business days. Retro template fields: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation applied, long-term fix owner, action items (owner + due date).
- Add recurring telemetry experiments to the platform-roadmap to reduce false positives: e.g., adaptive-baseline computation, window-aware anomaly detection, and cohort-based prefetch resilience.

Appendix: useful commands and example queries
- Operator telemetry query via curl:

  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/platform/telemetry/query -d '{"query":"SELECT percentile(0.99, token_latency_ms) FROM telemetry.tokens WHERE service=\\\"runtime-api\\\" AND time > now() - interval \'1 hour\'"}' | jq .

- Batcher status (JSON):

  cli operator batcher status --pool gpu-pool-2 --format json

- Notes on safe mitigation windows:
  - Preferred: 00:00–04:00 PT: automated mitigations permitted with operator approval.
  - Avoid invasive kernel restarts or model swaps between 02:00–03:00 PT when long-running scheduled jobs begin.
